newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NAB shares fall after competition warning.
newsitem.headline: NAB shares fall after competition warning.

text.p: The share price of Australia's largest and most profitable bank, National Australia Bank Ltd, fell sharply after it warned of more competition, traders said.
"I think people are still coming to grips with the results," said Paul Doherty, a dealer at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
"There are concerns about comments that competition increases pressure on sustaining record profit," Doherty said.

"Most of the good news seems to be have factored into the price," he said. NAB shares were 24 cents lower at A$18.10 at 2.00 p.m. (0400 GMT) and had struck a A$18.55 record high before the results were announced around midday.

NAB managing director Don Argus said in an accompanying statement that unrelenting competition in all markets would place increasing pressure on the bank's ability to sustain its run of record profits.
"Most of the comments that are accompanying the bank results are highlighting the difficulties with maintaining the same sorts of growth," said John Bowie Wilson at BNP Equities.
"That doesn't come as any great surprise to us. But that is just one thing that has to be taken into account," Bowie Wilson said.
"Westpac said it, St George has said it, NAB has now said it."
